Misbehaving Municipalities

By: Ntokozo Miya | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Following a first of its kind court ruling to have the Makana Municipality's council dissolved, we examine what this means for other communities struggling to have municipalities deliver services.

Unique Selling Point:
We speak to activists who have championed service delivery demands in their communities – some who brought court cases against their municipalities, some who stopped paying for services altogether and others who even took matters in their own hands by attempting to fix their towns themselves. How are things are allowed to deteriorate so badly?

Summary:
Following years of back-and-forths with the Makana Municipality over poor service delivery, the community took the matter to court to demand that the council be dissolved and new leadership be elected in hopes that things will improve. The court ruled in the residents' favour and for the first time ever, this decision could see an entire municipal council replaced. The ANC-led municipality is appealing the judgement. We examine the effect of this ruling on other communities with other problems – will they be inspired to intensify their efforts and possibly call for their own municipal councils to be dissolved?

Further information:
For years, sewerage has flowed freely on the streets of some areas in Makhanda (Grahamstown) and often, there is no water for days on end. After countless protests and interactions with municipal officials, residents felt their concerns were ignored. Led by the Unemployed People's Movement and other civil organisations including the Grahamstown Residents Association, the community headed to court, and won. The ruling is expected to inspire other communities to take to the courts and we speak to activists in other problem areas to determine this. We also clarify exactly happens when a council is dissolved – who is in charge until a new council is elected?

The story will be told through the eyes of activists around the country who have exhausted all efforts to get proper service delivery from their various municipalities, and failed. Some of them have even gone to court to demand reliable water supply, sanitation and better roads. In some of the cases, even when the courts rules in favour of the residents and orders that municipalities deliver those services, nothing happens. Out of frustration for paying for services they do not receive, some stop paying for utilities. In this part of the discussion, we also highlight stats on service delivery protests across country.

In the insert, we make mention of other areas, including Koster in the North West, that CB has covered in terms of service delivery failures and provide updates.The discussion also explores alternative political styles, financial audits on municipalities and the need for skilled management at municipal level.

Extra Budget Items:
Travel plan

Day 1 – Sunday 1 March 2020

Fly out of Johannesburg for P.E. Airport as early as possible on Sunday, Clayson (Eastern Cape cameraman) drives a big car and can pick us up from airport and we drive to Grahamstown together, spend day shooting and in the afternoon/evening, he'll drop us off at the airport for flight back to Johannesburg.

Travelers – Presenter, Ntokozo and Mdu

Day 2 – Monday 2 March 2020

Interview expert/analyst in Pretoria, pick up rental car and drive to North West – we'll arrive in North-West late because we will only get to interview Dr Brand in Pretoria at 2pm.

Travelers – Presenter, Ntokozo and Mdu

Day 3 – Tuesday 3 March 2020

North-West interviews and drive back to Johannesburg, return rental car.

Travelers – Presenter, Ntokozo and Mdu


Please help, in Grahamstown, we will shoot with Clayson who has shot an interview for us in the Eastern Cape before. We hoped to travel with a cameraman to the North-West but the people we normally shoot with are unavailable, please help and kindly suggest some if you have contacts. We are also speaking to other producers for those contacts.

Also, seeing as are a 2-person team, where necessary we will make payment for travel costs. Both Mdu and I plan to travel as he drives and also operates our new drones (handheld and flight) – we have spent so much on drone footage previously, it worked out cheaper to buy them.

Script:


MISBEHAVING MUNICIPALITIES SCRIPT – POST VIEWING

The quaint town of Grahamstown, known for its historical architecture and Arts Festival is in the Eastern Cape's Makana Municipality. For its roughly 70-thousand residents, service delivery is painfully lacking.
LINK - Roads that have seen better days, recurring power outages and blocked drainage systems – frustrated residents sacrifice their weekends and take matters into their own hands.
PHILLIPA IRVINE – MAKHANDA RESIDENT
CB - It's a Sunday afternoon and other people are having lunch, what are you doing out here?
PHILLIPA – We are here clearing this gutter that has been blocked for, it must be some years now.
VO – Resident Phillipa Irvine says locals took up tools because the town’s officials don't provide services.
PHILLIPA IRVINE – MAKHANDA RESIDENT
There is the river clean-up on the other side of town just to make sure that the infrastructure doesn't take as much strain as it's been taking.
VO – After years of protests, the frustrated Makhanda community went to court to make a bold demand.
Led by the Unemployed People's Movement - or UPM - residents asked that the entire municipal council be fired and new people elected.
LINK - In an unprecedented move in January, the high court in Makhanda ruled that the Makana municipality be dissolved and placed under administration over service delivery failures but what exactly does that mean?
VO – The online data and monitoring service Municipal IQ reports that two hundred and eighteen service delivery protests were recorded in 2019 across South Africa. The demonstrations are directly linked to how municipalities spend money. The Auditor-General audits and recommends steps to curb the misuse of state funds. For the year ending in June 2018, more than twenty-five billion rands was unaccounted for.
But Dr Dirk Brand who specialises in municipal management legislation at Stellenbosch University sees troubled municipalities routinely ignoring the Auditor-General’s recommendations.
DR DIRK BRAND – PUBLIC GOVERNANCE LECTURER
One gets the impression that there is a lack of accountability in many places in the country. One has to take the report of the Auditor-General seriously. It must be adhered to and there must be consequences.
VO – Many communities have gone to court to demand specific services, but this was the first time that residents submitted a plea to dismiss officials.
When a municipality is dissolved, provincial government steps in to pull a rescue.
DR DIRK BRAND – PUBLIC GOVERNANCE LECTURER
There would then be administrators coming in, appointed by the provincial government, to take control of the administration for a specific period of time. They have to report regularly to the provincial government and in that way there is a plan put in place to solve the issues.
VO – The UPM's Sikhumbuzo Soxujwa says the Makana Municipality failed the people.
SIKHUMBUZO SOXUJWA – UNEMPLOYED PEOPLE'S MOVEMENT
We have been complaining about corruption, collapse of infrastructure, sewage spills but they did not listen to us. That is why we decided to go to court because section 152 of the constitution says you can ask for a dissolution.
VO – The landmark ruling has inspired other communities.
SIKHUMBUZO SOXUJWA – UNEMPLOYED PEOPLE'S MOVEMENT
Residents of Komane, as we are speaking, they have taken their municipality for dissolution. We are engaging with the other activists of certain municipalities to do so.
VO – The municipality plans to appeal. In a statement, it wrote that it had “cost containment measures put in place to curb irregular, wasteful and fruitless expenditure”, and “a Financial Misconduct Disciplinary Board has also been established”.
LINK - Makhanda residents worry that the municipality's appeal means that they'll have to deal with battered roads, water shortages and sewage spills for some time to come.
VO – Since the ruling, little has changed in the area, says Professor Philip Machanick, chairperson of the Grahamstown Residents’ Association.
PROF PHILIP MACHANICK – GRAHAMSTOWN RESIDENTS’ ASSOCIATION
Unfortunately your viewers can't actually smell this but we are standing next to a stream of sewage and the sewage situation is extremely bad. On the other side of town the landfill site is an absolute disgrace.
VO – The dissolution case wasn't the municipality's first time before a judge. In 2015, the council was ordered to erect a fence around the local landfill and manage the filthy water flowing from the dump. But that didn't happen.
In a devastating blow in early March, a judge found the mayor and municipal manager in contempt of court. The pair has been sentenced to six months behind bars, which will be wholly suspended if they service the landfill within 30 days.
Daphne Timm, a real estate agent in Makhanda, says poor services have knocked the property market hard.
DAPHNE TIMM – PAM GOLDING PROPERTY GROUP
One property I can mention was sold for R4.75 million, huge renovations done to it, it has just been resold for R2.7 million. That's around half the price.
VO – We drove around the country to get people’s reaction to the Makhanda judgement.
Sixty kilometres south in the upmarket town of Kenton-on-Sea in the Ndlambe Municipality, George Poole, chairperson of the Ratepayers’ Association, says for them, dissolution is not yet an option, though they have gone to court to demand services.
GEORGE POOLE – KENTON-ON-SEA RATEPAYERS’ ASSOCIATION
We are lucky that we have a very good relationship certain sections of the municipality, but we find that with their best intentions, every now and again they appear to be blocked by their political superiors from doing what they want to do and what they should do.
VO - In 2016, the community demanded that a waste dump be relocated away from a residential area.
GEORGE POOLE – KENTON-ON-SEA RATEPAYERS ASSOCIATION
They eventually closed the dump and for the past 3 years they have been required to report back to the court every 3 months on what steps they have taken towards identifying and establishing a new dump and in fact they've made absolutely no progress.
VO – Our next stop was the North-West province where out of 4 district and 18 local municipalities, sixteen are under administration including the Tswaing Municipality.
LINK - It's all good and well to dissolve a municipality but residents here in the North West say a sure way to resolve the service delivery crisis is to appoint suitably qualified people to manage the municipalities.
VO – For residents of Delareyville in the Tswaing Municipality, potholes are costly and damaging - Buddy Anthony runs a trucking business in the area..
BUDDY ANTHONY – DELAREYVILLE RESIDENT
The truck stands for 2-3 hours before it's got a spare wheel on and then there is no way you can use that tyre again. Once a pothole hits it, it damages it. These tyres is about R4 000 to R4 500 before V.A.T.
VO – Persistent water shortage has also set him back thousands of rands.
BUDDY ANTHONY – DELAREYVILLE RESIDENT
The municipal water comes on 6 o'clock in the morning and by 8 o'clock, if you haven't wet your garden or filled up your tanks, you won't have water for the toilet or water to make food till the next morning.
VO – In neighbouring Ottosdal, also in the Tswaing municipality, we met ward councillor Linda Taljaard. She praised the people of Makhanda for taking a stand.
LINDA TALJAARD – OTTOSDAL WARD COUNCILLOR - CLIP – 0051XX
I think they are brilliant and I think that has to happen in the whole South Africa.
VO - Speaking to us outside the municipal offices which were set alight during a protest last year, she says council staff is not adequately qualified.
LINDA TALJAARD – OTTOSDAL WARD COUNCILLOR - CLIP – 0051XX
These people are totally incompetent. They can never be reached so services aren’t delivered. No-one oversees the workers who should be working under the municipal managers’ supervision.
DR DIRK BRAND – PUBLIC GOVERNANCE LECTURER
If you don't have the right qualified people in managing the finances, then that will also lead to a deterioration of the administration
VO – We tried to get comment from the various municipalities but none responded in time for this broadcast.
According to a 2018 Public Affairs Research Institute report, one hundred and forty municipalities have been placed under administration since 1998. Tshwane in Gauteng is the most recent entry on this list.
On the fifth of March, the province announced it would dissolve the municipality which was left without a leader after the resignation of former mayor Stevens Mokgalapa.
At a recent meeting about government's service delivery strategy, President Cyril Ramaphosa issued an ominous warning to municipal officials.
UPSOUND – PRESIDENT CYRIL RAMAPHOSA
Many of the challenges we face are our own making and the inevitable outcome of poor planning, fragmented implementation, poor oversight and monitoring, wastage and duplication. Unless we work smarter, all our best laid plans to accelerate service delivery will amount to naught.

PROMOS
Roads pockmarked with potholes, water shortages and sewage and litter on streets – frustrated residents take to the courts to demand services from their municipalities.

A first-of-its-kind court ruling to have a municipality dissolved over service delivery failures – will other communities be inspired to head to the courts to demand services?

A court has ruled that a municipality be dissolved over service delivery failures – will more communities take to the courts to demand basic services?

BUDDY ANTHONY – DELAREYVILLE RESIDENT The municipal water comes on 6 o'clock in the morning and by 8 o'clock, if you haven't wet your garden or filled up your tanks, you won't have water for the toilet or water to make food till the next morning. VO – In neighbouring Ottosdal, also in the Tswaing municipality, we met ward councillor Linda Taljaard. She praised the people of Makhanda for taking a stand. LINDA TALJAARD – OTTOSDAL WARD COUNCILLOR - CLIP – 0051XX I think they are brilliant and I think that has to happen in the whole South Africa. VO - Speaking to us outside the municipal offices which were set alight during a protest last year, she says council staff is not adequately qualified. LINDA TALJAARD – OTTOSDAL WARD COUNCILLOR - CLIP – 0051XX These people are totally incompetent. They can never be reached so services aren’t delivered. No-one oversees the workers who should be working under the municipal managers’ supervision. DR DIRK BRAND – PUBLIC GOVERNANCE LECTURER If you don't have the right qualified people in managing the finances, then that will also lead to a deterioration of the administration VO – We tried to get comment from the various municipalities but none responded in time for this broadcast. According to a 2018 Public Affairs Research Institute report, one hundred and forty municipalities have been placed under administration since 1998. Tshwane in Gauteng is the most recent entry on this list. On the fifth of March, the province announced it would dissolve the municipality which was left without a leader after the resignation of former mayor Stevens Mokgalapa. At a recent meeting about government's service delivery strategy, President Cyril Ramaphosa issued an ominous warning to municipal officials. UPSOUND – PRESIDENT CYRIL RAMAPHOSA Many of the challenges we face are our own making and the inevitable outcome of poor planning, fragmented implementation, poor oversight and monitoring, wastage and duplication. Unless we work smarter, all our best laid plans to accelerate service delivery will amount to naught. PROMOS Roads pockmarked with potholes, water shortages and sewage and litter on streets – frustrated residents take to the courts to demand services from their municipalities. A first-of-its-kind court ruling to have a municipality dissolved over service delivery failures – will other communities be inspired to head to the courts to demand services? A court has ruled that a municipality be dissolved over service delivery failures – will more communities take to the courts to demand basic services?

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Following a first of its kind court ruling to have the Makana Municipality's council dissolved, we examine what this means for other communities struggling to have municipalities deliver services.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We speak to activists who have championed service delivery demands in their communities – some who brought court cases against their municipalities, some who stopped paying for services altogether and others who even took matters in their own hands by attempting to fix their towns themselves. How are things are allowed to deteriorate so badly?
metadata.Summary: Following years of back-and-forths with the Makana Municipality over poor service delivery, the community took the matter to court to demand that the council be dissolved and new leadership be elected in hopes that things will improve. The court ruled in the residents' favour and for the first time ever, this decision could see an entire municipal council replaced. The ANC-led municipality is appealing the judgement. We examine the effect of this ruling on other communities with other problems – will they be inspired to intensify their efforts and possibly call for their own municipal councils to be dissolved?
metadata.Further information: For years, sewerage has flowed freely on the streets of some areas in Makhanda (Grahamstown) and often, there is no water for days on end. After countless protests and interactions with municipal officials, residents felt their concerns were ignored. Led by the Unemployed People's Movement and other civil organisations including the Grahamstown Residents Association, the community headed to court, and won. The ruling is expected to inspire other communities to take to the courts and we speak to activists in other problem areas to determine this. We also clarify exactly happens when a council is dissolved – who is in charge until a new council is elected? The story will be told through the eyes of activists around the country who have exhausted all efforts to get proper service delivery from their various municipalities, and failed. Some of them have even gone to court to demand reliable water supply, sanitation and better roads. In some of the cases, even when the courts rules in favour of the residents and orders that municipalities deliver those services, nothing happens. Out of frustration for paying for services they do not receive, some stop paying for utilities. In this part of the discussion, we also highlight stats on service delivery protests across country. In the insert, we make mention of other areas, including Koster in the North West, that CB has covered in terms of service delivery failures and provide updates.The discussion also explores alternative political styles, financial audits on municipalities and the need for skilled management at municipal level.
